title: The Vine, the Branches, and Love
overview: On the night before his arrest, Jesus tells his closest followers to stay joined to him like branches on a vine, to love each other as he has loved them, and to expect hostility from those who reject him.

parts.label: The vine and the gardener (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The Hebrew scriptures often pictured Israel as a vine God planted, so Jesus calling himself the true vine presents him as what that picture pointed to, with God as the gardener. Pruning trims growth that holds a plant back, and in Greek the word for pruning sounds like the word for clean: his teaching has already trimmed and prepared them.

parts.label: Staying connected (vv. 4-8)
parts.note: To remain in him means staying joined to him, the way a branch draws its life from the vine. Interpreters read the fruit as a good and loving life, as new followers won through their work, or as both, and the branch thrown on the fire is a stark image whose meaning Christians debate.

parts.label: Remain in my love (vv. 9-17)
parts.note: Jesus says he loves them as the Father loves him, and his command is that they love each other the same way, even to the point of giving their lives. He calls them friends, not servants, because he has shared his purposes with them, and Christians read verse 13 as pointing to his own death the next day.

parts.label: When the world hates you (vv. 18-25)
parts.note: In this book, "the world" means people and powers set against God, not the planet, and Jesus warns that his followers will be treated as he was. Those who saw his works and heard his words and still turned on him have no excuse, and he echoes a Psalm about enemies whose hatred had no grounds.

parts.label: Two witnesses to come (vv. 26-27)
parts.note: Jesus promises to send the Spirit of truth from the Father, using a Greek word for someone called to stand beside you, like a helper or a defender in court. The Spirit will speak up for Jesus, and so will these followers, because they have been with him from the start.

disagreement: Christians differ over whether the branches cut off and burned (vv. 2, 6) are genuine believers who can fall away and be lost, or people who only seemed to be connected to Jesus and never truly were.
think: Jesus links lasting good in a life to staying connected to its source. What connections in your own life genuinely produce good in you, and which ones only look like they do?
